KreateWebsites for enterprise customers: creation, migration, content operations and the path to intelligent digital experiences.

Explore the presentation

One lifecycle, from publishing to participation

The deck presents a progressive approach: modernize an existing website, structure content and catalogs, connect personal customer actions, introduce AI assistance, and improve the experience through measured experiments.

KREATE supports building and delivery; KONTROLS adds governance and evidence; KNOBS connects changes to outcomes. The reference architecture separates public delivery from application services and controlled release operations.

Capability maturity matters

The presentation distinguishes implemented or reported capabilities from pilots, hardening work and planned capabilities. Slide 19 preserves this breakdown. Migration coverage, customer-specific integrations, SLAs and control commitments are scoped separately.

Slide 7 of 20

Migration Fidelity and Control

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
M O D E R N I Z E Migration designed around fidelity and control Reduce dependence on the old platform while preserving pages, assets and customer pathways. KREATEWEBSITES / DATAKNOBS 07 1 Discover > 2 Capture > 3 Transform > 4 Validate > 5 Preview > 6 Publish Protect the assets Import images, CSS, scripts and downloads; rewrite URLs to controlled storage. Prove the outcome Compare links and appearance, surface missing dependencies, keep a report. Cut over safely Review preview, validate DNS and preserve a recoverable deployment snapshot. Connector coverage and automated validation depth are being hardened; do not assume universal one-click migration.

Frequently asked questions

What does the KreateWebsites enterprise platform cover?

The presentation covers website creation and migration, CMS and publishing, structured catalogs, personal customer actions, AI assistance, governance and experimentation.

How do KREATE, KONTROLS and KNOBS fit together?

KREATE builds and delivers experiences. KONTROLS defines policies, reviews and evidence. KNOBS supports experiments, measurement and controlled rollout. AI and KreateBots add assistance and engagement.

Must visitors sign in to read public content?

The deck keeps public reading and discovery open and indexable. Sign-in is introduced for personal actions such as saving places, collections and tracking a journey.

Are all presented capabilities fully released?

No. Slide 19 distinguishes implemented or reported capabilities, pilot and hardening work, and designed or in-progress capabilities. Release scope and deployment commitments require validation.

How does an enterprise start?

The proposed sequence is assess, pilot, validate and scale. Begin with a narrow website, migration, catalog or personalized journey and measure the outcome before expanding.
